FMFN ELDER NEWS
FMFN Elders Thanksgiving
On October 6th, the FMFN Elders enjoyed
their Thanksgiving lunch and bingo, and
here are some photos from the event.
The menu was the traditional ‘Turkey and
fixings,’ and the door prizes were two 32-inch
television sets. Bingo prizes included all manner
of kitchen appliances, including a crock pot,
waffle maker, a pan big enough to cook a
turkey, an indoor grill and many more. For the
handi-person there was a Mastercraft tool set, a
shopvac and even an axe suitable for the tallest
of trees.
Thank you to the Elders Services team for
another magnificent event. It looks like they all
had fun.

FMFN SPORTS NEWS
Northern Spirits in Flag Football Event
The Fort McKay Northern Spirits have
expanded their sporting repertoire, taking
part in their first Flag Football event. The
results were mixed, but coach Dylan Fougere
was happy with the event and the enthusiasm
shown by the team. The girls participating in the
First Football Alberta Flag Football Tournament,
placed sixth of eighteen teams, getting knocked
out first round of playoffs by Strathcona.
Competing were:
Mya Wilson
Leanne Grandjambe
Neah Boucher
Michelle Bouchier
Geanna Grandjambe
Angel Ward
Malibu Grandjambe
Airabella Cardinal
Faith & Sienna Deschambeault
Flag football is a variant of football where,
instead of tackling players to the ground, the
defensive team must remove a flag or flag
belt from the ball carrier (“deflagging”) to end
a down. Contact is therefore limited between
players, making it a fun and fast game. Flag
football will be a discretionary event for the 2028
Summer Olympics in Los Angeles.

Handy Home Maintenance Course
On October 7th & 8th, the Housing department put on a two-day course aimed at teaching
younger community members and future home occupants some useful skills when it comes
to dealing with household issues. The Members Basic Home Maintenance Workshop dealt
with the matters in a hands-on manner, and our camera caught the students while they were
learning all about the plumbing of a toilet. Fortunately, the facility in question was not connected to
anything, so the art of unblocking the pipes remained a theoretical, and clean, lesson.
Kaydence is our Number One!
Congratulations to local singer and Hip-Hop Artist Kaydence Gladue. Her new hit song, Beaded
Earrings with Jessa Sky was number one on the Indigenous Countdown charts. Kaydence is
an emerging Indigenous hip-hop and R&B artist whose music blends confidence, culture, and
authentic storytelling. Known for tracks like THAT GURL, RezzyWrld, Love Song, and DIFFERENCE,
Kaydence has quickly built a name for herself with bold lyricism, infectious energy, and a growing
catalogue of collaborations that celebrate Indigenous identity and modern Indigenous excellence.

FMFN CHIEF & COUNCIL NEWS
First Nations-First Ministers’ Meeting
On October 26, Chief Raymond Powder
represented Fort McKay First Nation at
the First Nations-First Ministers’ Meeting
in Ottawa. The gathering brought First Nations
leaders together with the Prime Minister and
provincial and territorial leaders for the first
meeting of its kind in roughly two decades.
For Fort McKay, having its own voice at the table
was essential. Chief Powder attended on behalf
of members and brought the Nation’s priorities
and experiences directly into the national
conversation. Leaders discussed Treaty rights,
economic opportunities, major projects and the
future of First Nations communities.
Chief Powder also delivered a letter to the Prime
Minister outlining the Nation’s priorities. These
included protecting Treaty rights, ensuring
meaningful involvement in decisions affecting
First Nations lands, supporting responsible
regional development and addressing the
cumulative effects that development projects
can have on communities.
Leaders also began discussing a proposed First
Nations Sovereign Wealth Fund. This tool could
help First Nations build shared ownership and
long-term wealth through investments.

FMFN EDUCATION NEWS
Moose Lake Trip - September 21st - 25th, 2026
Back in September, our Land-Based
Learning program took students beyond
the classroom with our first-ever Moose
Lake on-the-land camp on Fort McKay’s
traditional territory. Highlights included the
moose harvest, hunting, fishing, boating,
canoeing, and berry picking. Students had
time to slow down, explore, ask questions, and
share stories while learning about gathering,
harvesting, and respecting Mother Nature.
Through hands-on experiences and the
guidance of Elders and Knowledge Keepers,
students deepened their understanding of
traditional ways and the importance of caring
for the land. The camp offered opportunities to
build relationships, learn from one another, and
create lasting memories. It reminded us that
some of the most meaningful learning happens
beyond the classroom. A heartfelt thank-you
to our volunteers, parents, chaperones, Elders
and Knowledge Keepers, cooks, helpers, Park
Rangers, Sustainability and Public Works staff,
and EFS staff and support team. Your time, care,
hard work, and shared knowledge made this
camp a memorable success. We are grateful to
everyone who helped bring traditional learning
to life through culture, connection, and time on
the land!

FMFN EDUCATION NEWS
Truth and Reconciliation Day – October 2nd, 2026
On October 2, Elsie Fabian School held its
annual Truth and Reconciliation Walk
in recognition of the National Day for
Truth and Reconciliation. We were honoured
to welcome students, staff, leaders, and
community members for a meaningful day of
remembrance, reflection, and unity. Together,
we honoured residential school Survivors, the
children who never returned home, and the
families and communities affected. A heartfelt
thank-you to the Cree and Dene drummers for
sharing their music and ceremony in the spirit of
reconciliation. Their contributions helped create
a powerful sense of connection and respect. The
event concluded with a round dance and a walk
together through the neighbourhood. Gathering
as a community reminded us of the importance
of listening, learning, and continuing to work
toward reconciliation together.
